cases.question: What is COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture about?
cases.standalone_question: What is COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture about?
cases.answer_excerpt:
COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture is a 3.0-credit course that focuses on the design, development, and management of web APIs.

The course covers the following key areas:
*   **RESTful APIs:** You will learn what RESTful APIs are, why they are important, and how to apply REST constraints and best practices.
*   **Core Concepts:** The curriculum explores the relationship between HTTP and REST, the use of HTTP status codes, and the implementation of CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations.
*   **Practical Skills:** You will gain experience in designing simple web services, documenting specifications, implementing error handling, and securing backend API servers.
*   **Technical Implementation:** The course involves working with REST, JSON, and HTTP, as well as applying change management and versioning to your API designs.

This course is part of the Computer Systems Technology Diploma program. Please note that it requires the completion of COMP 1537 and COMP 3522 as prerequisites.

Sources:
- https://www.bcit.ca/courses/internet-software-architecture-comp-4537/
- https://www.bcit.ca/programs/computer-systems-technology-diploma-full-time-5500dipma/
- https://www.bcit.ca/outlines/20261088086/
sub_queries: COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture course description and topics

cases.question: What are the three main topic areas covered in COMP 1113 Applied Mathematics?
cases.standalone_question: What are the three main topic areas covered in COMP 1113 Applied Mathematics?
cases.answer_excerpt:
The course COMP 1113, Applied Mathematics, is divided into the following three main topic areas:

*   **Boolean algebra and the design of logic circuits:** This includes concepts such as Boolean variables, operators, truth tables, canonical forms, and simplification using mathematical proofs and Karnaugh maps.
*   **Number systems and data representation:** This covers positional number systems and how various data types—including numbers, text, and graphics—are represented within a computer, as well as performing arithmetic operations in different bases (binary, octal, and hexadecimal).
*   **Functions, linear equations, vectors, and matrices:** This involves solving systems of linear equations using algebraic methods, determinants, and matrices, as well as performing basic matrix operations.

Sources:
https://www.bcit.ca/courses/applied-mathematics-comp-1113/
https://www.bcit.ca/outlines/20261048068/

cases.question: Am I automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan, and can I opt out?
cases.standalone_question: Am I automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan, and can I opt out?
cases.answer_excerpt:
You are automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan if you are a student in a program designated as full-time by BCIT that lasts at least 16 weeks. The fee for this plan is automatically included in your tuition upon registration.

Regarding the opt-out process:

*   **Eligibility to Opt-Out:** You may opt out of the plan if you already have comparable extended health and dental coverage through another provider (such as an employer, parent, or spouse).
*   **Deadline:** You must submit your opt-out request within 30 days of the start of your program. This can be done once every 12 months.
*   **Process:** After the 30-day deadline, opt-outs cannot be processed. For specific instructions on how to submit your request, you should visit the BCITSA Student Plan website or contact the BCITSA Health & Dental Plan Office located in building SE2 on the Burnaby campus.

**3) Burnaby Campus Student Housing**
BCIT offers student housing on the Burnaby campus with over 800 rooms available:
*   **Tall Timber Student Housing:** Opened in Fall 2025, this facility offers fully self-contained Studio rooms and Connected Single rooms.
*   **Townhouses:** These are legacy units that host 12 students each in private rooms with shared common facilities.

Please note that housing is not guaranteed, and it is recommended that you apply early through the official website.

cases.question: Which English proficiency categories does BCIT use for admissions?
cases.follow_up: What TOEFL iBT score does Category 2 require?
cases.standalone_question: What TOEFL iBT score does BCIT English proficiency Category 2 require?

prior_turns.question: Which English proficiency categories does BCIT use for admissions?

cases.answer_excerpt:
The TOEFL iBT score required for Category 2 depends on when you take the test:

*   **Prior to January 21, 2026:** An overall score of 86 is required, with no section score less than 20.
*   **As of January 21, 2026:** An overall score of 4.5 is required, with a minimum score of 3.5 in each of the Speaking, Writing, Reading, and Listening sections.

Please note that for assessment tests, your results must be dated no more than two years before your program start date.
